In 2026, the public will see ten new exhibitions, including monographic exhibitions by Julie Mehretu, Maria Jarema, and Edward Dwurnik. There are also plans for an extensive presentation of world sculpture and an international exhibition devoted to surrealism. We will also invite the Museum's audience to participate in an extensive public, cinema, and educational program. The Museum's branches: the House in Szumin, the Dance Pavilion, and the Sculpture Park in Bródno will be working intensively.

…

At the beginning of summer, a comprehensive international exhibition entitled *In the Very Bowels of Change: Surrealism and Anti-Fascism* will open at the beginning of summer, first presented from October 15 to March 30, 2025, at the Lenbachhaus in Munich under the title: *But Live Here? No Thanks: Surrealism and Anti-Fascism*

…

MSN continues its mission of making art available to the widest possible audience, free of charge, thanks to Gallery A, located on the ground floor and fully visible from Marszałkowska Street. The Museum also values its close connection with the Polish art world, which is why throughout 2026, the ground floor will showcase the work of experimental Polish artists of the younger generation. On January 29, an exhibition prepared by Łukasz Ronduda (MSN) entitled Misterioso Nadii Markiewicz will open. Markiewicz is an artist interested in creating a new image of disability that refers to categories such as mystery and uniqueness. April will see the first institutional presentation of the work of Przemysław Piniak, a prematurely deceased intermedia artist (curatorial team: Szymon Maliborski, Gabriela Skrzypczak, Przemysław Sowiński). In July, Gallery A will feature paintings by Adam Kozicki, an artist inspired by the frenetic pace of the modern internet (curator: Natalia Sielewicz). Admission to the ground floor of the museum is free thanks to cooperation with Audi."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://publicznosc.artmuseum.pl/en/wydarzenia/2026","title":"Events - Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw","description":"The Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw is a national cultural institution established in 2005, located at in the very center of Warsaw. In 2026 we plan to expand this deliberative character in building the museum’s program—first and foremost by inviting diverse organizations and individuals to help create the program for the publicly accessible, free-admission space on the ground floor. The exhibition schedule for the new year is constructed in a similar spirit. Several new exhibitions, dialoguing with one another, should make a visit to the museum an unforgettable experience of the pulse of modernity—multifaceted, intense, sometimes chaotic, but also offering signposts. Two exhibitions that opened last year are still underway: the monumental *The Woman Question 1550–2025* and *The City of Women*. In mid-March 2026 we will open two one-woman shows, of Maria Jarema (1908–1958) and of Julie Mehretu, who was born in 1970 in Addis Ababa. Two visions of abstract painting and political engagement, from a Polish avant-gardist and from a multi-ethnic artist who has renewed American abstract expressionism and become one of the most influential artists of our times. In June, the exhibition *You Are at the Heart of Change: Surrealism and Anti-fascism*

…

This year, Gallery A on the ground floor (free admission) will present profiles of experimental Polish artists of the younger generation. Nadia Markiewicz’s exhibition *Misterioso* will open on 29 January. Subsequent shows in that space will feature Przemysław Piniak and Adam Kozicki. There will be another edition of the Warsaw Under Construction festival, with numerous events devoted to urban design and improving city spaces. The museum’s surroundings are also developing—this summer a sculpture by Dominika Olszowy, *Monument of a Fountain*, will be erected in the Central Square next to the MSN Warsaw building."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://msl.org.pl/en","title":"Strona główna | Muzeum Sztuki w Łodzi","description":"Please note: In connection with ... 2026, to Saturday, 7 November 2026. results.title: Plans for 2026
results.description: Exhibitions, accompanying events, ... 2026, the public will see ten new exhibitions, including monographic exhibitions by Julie Mehretu, Maria Jarema, and Edward Dwurnik....

highlights:
[Plans for 2026]

In 2026, the public will see ten new exhibitions, including monographic exhibitions by Julie Mehretu, Maria Jarema, and Edward Dwurnik. There are also plans for an extensive presentation of world sculpture and an international exhibition devoted to surrealism. We will also invite the Museum's audience to participate in an extensive public, cinema, and educational program. The Museum's branches: the House in Szumin, the Dance Pavilion, and the Sculpture Park in Bródno will be working intensively.

…

At the beginning of summer, a comprehensive international exhibition entitled *In the Very Bowels of Change: Surrealism and Anti-Fascism* will open at the beginning of summer, first presented from October 15 to March 30, 2025, at the Lenbachhaus in Munich under the title: *But Live Here? No Thanks: Surrealism and Anti-Fascism*

…

MSN continues its mission of making art available to the widest possible audience, free of charge, thanks to Gallery A, located on the ground floor and fully visible from Marszałkowska Street. The Museum also values its close connection with the Polish art world, which is why throughout 2026, the ground floor will showcase the work of experimental Polish artists of the younger generation. On January 29, an exhibition prepared by Łukasz Ronduda (MSN) entitled Misterioso Nadii Markiewicz will open. Markiewicz is an artist interested in creating a new image of disability that refers to categories such as mystery and uniqueness. April will see the first institutional presentation of the work of Przemysław Piniak, a prematurely deceased intermedia artist (curatorial team: Szymon Maliborski, Gabriela Skrzypczak, Przemysław Sowiński). In July, Gallery A will feature paintings by Adam Kozicki, an artist inspired by the frenetic pace of the modern internet (curator: Natalia Sielewicz). Admission to the ground floor of the museum is free thanks to cooperation with Audi.

highlights:
[Letter from Joanna Mytkowska, director of MSN]

In 2026 we plan to expand this deliberative character in building the museum’s program—first and foremost by inviting diverse organizations and individuals to help create the program for the publicly accessible, free-admission space on the ground floor. The exhibition schedule for the new year is constructed in a similar spirit. Several new exhibitions, dialoguing with one another, should make a visit to the museum an unforgettable experience of the pulse of modernity—multifaceted, intense, sometimes chaotic, but also offering signposts. Two exhibitions that opened last year are still underway: the monumental *The Woman Question 1550–2025* and *The City of Women*. In mid-March 2026 we will open two one-woman shows, of Maria Jarema (1908–1958) and of Julie Mehretu, who was born in 1970 in Addis Ababa. Two visions of abstract painting and political engagement, from a Polish avant-gardist and from a multi-ethnic artist who has renewed American abstract expressionism and become one of the most influential artists of our times. In June, the exhibition *You Are at the Heart of Change: Surrealism and Anti-fascism*

…

This year, Gallery A on the ground floor (free admission) will present profiles of experimental Polish artists of the younger generation. Nadia Markiewicz’s exhibition *Misterioso* will open on 29 January. Subsequent shows in that space will feature Przemysław Piniak and Adam Kozicki. There will be another edition of the Warsaw Under Construction festival, with numerous events devoted to urban design and improving city spaces. The museum’s surroundings are also developing—this summer a sculpture by Dominika Olszowy, *Monument of a Fountain*, will be erected in the Central Square next to the MSN Warsaw building.
